items.t: Prophylaxis of angina pectoris. Not for relief of an acute angina attack (use sublingual GTN).

src.q: Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets is indicated for the prophylaxis of angina pectoris.
Imdur is not indicated for relief of acute angina attacks

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction or brand-specific prescribing statement found in the SmPCs used; no MHRA or SPS brand-prescribing advice found.

items.t: Immediate-release: one tablet two or three times a day, taken asymmetrically to allow a nitrate-low period. Nitrate-naive: start 20 mg twice daily. Usual maintenance 20-120 mg daily; use the lowest effective dose.

src.q: One tablet to be taken asymmetrically (to allow a nitrate low period) two or three times a day.
it is recommended that the initial dose be one tablet of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg twice a day.
The maintenance dose in individual patients is usually between 20- 120 mg daily.

items.t: MR tablets: 60 mg once daily in the morning; may increase to 120 mg (two tablets) once daily in the morning. To reduce headache, may start with 30 mg (half a tablet) for the first 2-4 days.

src.q: Imdur 60mg (one tablet) once daily given in the morning. The dose may be increased to 120mg (two tablets) daily, both to be taken once daily in the morning.
The dose can be titrated to minimise the possibility of headache, by initiating treatment with 30mg (half a tablet) for the first 2-4 days.

items.t: MR capsules: one or two capsules daily in the morning; use the lowest effective dose. If effect wanes on prolonged-release treatment, intermittent therapy may be more suitable.

src.q: One capsule to be taken daily, or two capsules daily, in the morning.
Attenuation of effect has occurred in some patients being treated with prolonged release preparations. In such patients intermittent therapy may be more appropriate

items.t: Do not stop suddenly; taper dose and frequency gradually.

src.q: Treatment with Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets, as with any other nitrates, should not be stopped suddenly. Both the dosage and frequency should be tapered gradually
Treatment with Elantan LA, as with any other nitrate, should not be stopped suddenly.

items.t: Elderly: no routine adjustment, but special care if prone to hypotension or with marked hepatic or renal insufficiency.

src.q: No evidence of a need for routine dosage adjustment in older people has been found, but special care may be needed in those with increased susceptibility to hypotension or marked hepatic or renal insufficiency.

items.t: Safety and efficacy in children not established (all three SmPCs).

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg has yet to be established in children.
The safety and efficacy of Imdur in children has not yet been established.
The safety and efficacy of Elantan LA has yet to be established in children.

items.t: With PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - all formulations.

src.q: their co-administration with nitrates or nitric oxide donors is therefore contraindicated
Patients treated with Imdur must not be given Phosphodiesterase Type 5 Inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil).

items.t: Hypersensitivity to isosorbide mononitrate (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules: also other nitrates; immediate-release tablets: also isosorbide dinitrate).

src.q: This product should not be given to patients with a known hypersensitivity to isosorbide dinitrate or mononitrate, to other nitrates or to any of the excipients.
Hypersensitivity to the active substance, other nitrates or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR capsules: acute MI with low filling pressures; acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse); very low blood pressure; HOCM; constrictive pericarditis; cardiac tamponade; low filling pressures; aortic/mitral stenosis; raised intracranial pressure (e.g. head trauma, cerebral haemorrhage); severe anaemia; closed-angle glaucoma; severe hypotension; hypovolaemia; toxic pulmonary oedema (immediate-release); riociguat.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg should not be used in cases of acute myocardial infarction with low filling pressures, acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse), or very low blood pressure
aortic/mitral valve stenosis and diseases associated with a raised intra-cranial pressure e.g. following a head trauma and including cerebral haemorrhage.
Elantan LA should not be used in patients with severe anaemia, closed angle glaucoma, severe hypotension or severe hypovolaemia.
should not be used in patients with marked anaemia, sever hypotension, closed angle glaucoma, toxic pulmonary oedema or hypovolaemia.

items.t: MR tablets: constrictive cardiomyopathy and pericarditis, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, mitral stenosis, severe anaemia.

src.q: Constrictive cardiomyopathy and pericarditis, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, mitral stenosis and severe anaemia.

items.t: Relative contraindications (immediate-release tablets and MR tablets): severe cerebrovascular insufficiency or hypotension.

src.q: Severe cerebrovascular insufficiency or hypotension are relative contraindications to the use of Imdur.

items.t: Use with caution after recent myocardial infarction, and in hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, severe liver or renal disease (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules). MR capsules: avoid lowering systolic BP below 90 mmHg.

src.q: should be used with caution in patients who have a recent history of myocardial infarction, or who are suffering from closed-angle glaucoma, hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition and sever liver or renal disease.
Reducing systolic blood-pressure below 90 mmHg must be avoided.

items.t: Postural hypotension and syncope can occur; circulatory collapse may follow the first dose with labile circulation (immediate-release: also in patients already on ACE inhibitors). Nitrate hypotension may come with paradoxical bradycardia and worse angina.

src.q: Symptoms of circulatory collapse may arise after first dose in patients with labile circulation and in patients already taking ACE inhibitors.
Hypotension induced by nitrates may be accompanied by paradoxical bradycardia and increased angina.

items.t: Tolerance and cross-tolerance to other nitrates can develop if not taken as directed (immediate-release: keep the asymmetric nitrate-low period). Avoid continuously high doses (MR capsules).

src.q: If the tablets are not taken as indicated (see section 4.2) tolerance to the medication and cross-tolerance to other nitrates may occur.
Continuously high dosages should be avoided.

items.t: MR capsules: caution in hypoxaemia and ventilation/perfusion imbalance (lung disease, ischaemic heart failure). Fast gastrointestinal transit may reduce release from MR formulations.

src.q: Caution should be exercised in patients with hypoxaemia and ventilation/perfusion imbalance due to lung disease or ischaemic heart failure.
In patients with decreased gastrointestinal transit time, and using prolonged-release formulation of isosorbide mononitrate, a decrease in release of the active ingredient may occur.

items.t: MR capsules: do not interrupt nitrate therapy in order to take a PDE5 inhibitor (risk of angina attack).

src.q: Elantan therapy should not be interrupted to take phosphodiesterase inhibitor-containing products (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil), because the risk of inducing an attack of angina pectoris could increase by doing so

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR capsules contain lactose and sucrose: patients with rare hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take them.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Due to the presence of sucrose, patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil): potentiate hypotension; possible syncope, MI or life-threatening cardiovascular complications. Must not be used together.

src.q: Patients who are on Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets therapy therefore must not use phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors.
Imdur and Phosphodiesterase Type 5 Inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil) must not be given concomitantly.

items.t: Blood-pressure-lowering medicines (beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, vasodilators, ARBs, ACE inhibitors), neuroleptics, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol may increase the hypotensive effect. MR capsules: if the BP fall with ACE inhibitors or arterial vasodilators is excessive, consider reducing one or both doses.

src.q: Concurrent administration of drugs with blood pressure lowering properties, e.g, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, vasodilators, alprostadil, aldesleukin, angiotensin II receptor antagonist, ACE inhibitors etc. may potentiate the hypotensive effect

The concurrent intake of ISMN with ACE-inhibitors or arterial vasodilators could be a desirable interaction unless the antihypertensive effects are excessive in which case consider reducing the dose of one or both drugs.

items.t: Riociguat: contraindicated (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules). Dihydroergotamine: levels and hypertensive effect may rise.

src.q: The use of isosorbide mononitrate with riociguat, a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase, is contra-indicated
may increase the blood level of dihydroergotamine and its hypertensive effect.

items.t: Immediate-release SmPC: reduce the dose in renal impairment (no threshold given); use with caution in severe renal disease.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

items.t: MR capsules: use with caution in severe renal disease. MR tablets: special care in older people with marked renal insufficiency. No numeric renal thresholds in any SmPC used.

src.q: Also in patients who are suffering from hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, severe liver or severe renal disease.
special care may be needed in those with increased susceptibility to hypotension or marked hepatic or renal insufficiency

items.t: Immediate-release SmPC: reduce the dose in hepatic impairment; caution in severe liver disease.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

items.t: MR capsules: caution in severe liver disease. MR tablets: special care in older people with marked hepatic insufficiency.

src.q: severe liver or severe renal disease
marked hepatic or renal insufficiency

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR tablets: safety and efficacy in pregnancy not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.
The safety and efficacy of Imdur during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.

items.t: MR capsules: no data suggesting harm, but safety not established; use only if the physician judges benefit outweighs possible hazard.

src.q: Isosorbide mononitrate should only be used in pregnancy and during lactation if, in the opinion of the physician, the possible benefits outweigh the possible hazards.

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR tablets: safety in lactation not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.

items.t: MR capsules: unknown whether nitrates pass into milk; use caution. No SPS breastfeeding page for nitrates was found.

src.q: It is not known whether nitrates are excreted in human milk and therefore caution should be exercised when administered to nursing women.

items.t: Fertility: no human data (MR capsules).

src.q: There is no data available on the effect of isosorbide mononitrate on fertility in humans.

items.t: Very common: throbbing headache (usually fades after 1-3 weeks). Common: hypotension or light-headedness on standing (especially at start or after a dose increase), dizziness, tachycardia, nausea (MR tablets), somnolence and asthenia (MR capsules).

src.q: A very common (>10% of patients) adverse reaction to Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets is throbbing headache.
At the start of therapy or when the dosage is increased, hypotension and/or light headedness in the upright position are commonly observed
Nervous system disorders Common Headache, dizziness
Cardiac and vascular disorders Common Hypotension, tachycardia Gastrointestinal disorders Common Nausea
very common: headache, common: dizziness (including dizziness postural), somnolence.

items.t: Uncommon: collapse (sometimes with bradyarrhythmia and syncope); severe hypotension that may worsen angina.

src.q: Uncommonly collapse may occur (sometimes accompanied by bradyarrhythmia and syncope). Uncommonly severe hypotension may lead to enhanced angina symptoms.

items.t: Rare/single cases: exfoliative dermatitis; angioedema (MR capsules, frequency not known). Nitrate-induced pituitary apoplexy reported in undiagnosed pituitary tumours.

src.q: In single cases exfoliative dermatitis may occur.
Immune system disorders: not known: angioedema
Nitrate-induced pituitary apoplexy has been reported in patients with undiagnosed pituitary tumours.

monitoring.note: No laboratory or routine monitoring stated in the SmPCs used; no SPS monitoring page found for nitrates.

items.t: Immediate-release: swallow whole with a drink of water; asymmetric dosing to leave a nitrate-low period.

src.q: It is recommended that the tablets should be swallowed whole with a drink of water.

items.t: MR tablets: do not chew or crush; swallow whole with half a glass of water, in the morning. The empty tablet matrix may be seen in the stool.

src.q: Imdur Tablets must not be chewed or crushed. They should be swallowed whole with half a glass of water.
Very occasionally the matrix may pass through the gastrointestinal tract without disintegrating and be found visible in the stool

items.t: MR capsules: take in the morning.

src.q: One capsule to be taken daily, or two capsules daily, in the morning.

items.t: Never take sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil (erectile dysfunction medicines) with this medicine.

src.q: Patients who undergo a maintenance treatment with Elantan should be informed that they must not use phosphodiesterase inhibitor-containing products (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil).

items.t: Use a GTN spray or sublingual tablet for an acute angina attack; this medicine does not treat attacks.

src.q: In the event of an acute angina attack, sublingual treatment such as a GTN spray or tablet should be used instead of isosorbide mononitrate tablets.

items.t: Avoid alcohol (severe postural hypotension). Dizziness, tiredness or blurred vision at the start may affect driving.

src.q: Severe postural hypotension with light headedness and dizziness is frequently observed after the consumption of alcohol, therefore alcohol should be avoided during treatment.
Dizziness, tiredness or blurred vision might occur at the start of treatment.

items.t: Headache is common at first and usually settles within 1-3 weeks. Do not stop suddenly.

src.q: The incidence of headache diminishes gradually or disappears after 1-3 weeks
Each tablet contains 100 micrograms Levothyroxine sodium anhydrous.

formulations.label: Oral solution
formulations.note: Monitor closely when switching between oral solution and tablets.

src.q: Each 5ml of oral solution contains 100micrograms Levothyroxine Sodium
Patients switching from the oral solution to the tablet form or from the tablet form to the oral solution should be monitored closely.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Hypothyroidism, including congenital hypothyroidism in infants, acquired hypothyroidism in children and juvenile myxoedema.

src.q: Control of hypothyroidism, congenital hypothyroidism in infants , acquired hypothyroidism in children and juvenile myxoedema.

items.t: Hypothyroidism (congenital or acquired); diffuse non-toxic goitre; goitre with Hashimoto's thyroiditis; suppression therapy in thyroid carcinoma.

src.q: i) hypothyroidism (congenital or acquired) ii) diffuse non toxic goitre iii) goitre associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis iv) Suppression therapy in thyroid carcinoma

items.t: Generic prescribing remains appropriate for most patients (MHRA). If a patient is persistently symptomatic after switching products, consider consistently prescribing a specific well-tolerated product; if problems persist, consider an oral solution.

src.q: generic prescribing of levothyroxine remains appropriate for the majority of patients
consider consistently prescribing a specific levothyroxine product known to be well tolerated by the patient
if symptoms or poor control of thyroid function persist despite adhering to a specific product, consider prescribing levothyroxine in an oral solution formulation

items.t: Not for weight reduction; large doses can cause serious or life-threatening effects, especially with sympathomimetic weight-loss products.

src.q: Thyroid hormones should not be given for weight reduction.

items.t: Adults under 50 years: start 100 micrograms daily, before breakfast. Increase by 50 micrograms every 3 to 4 weeks until stable. Usual final dose 100 to 200 micrograms daily.

src.q: Patients under 50 years age: Initially 100 micrograms daily, preferably taken before breakfast or the first meal of the day.
Adjust at three to four week intervals by 50 micrograms until normal metabolism is steadily maintained. The final daily dose may be up to 100 to 200 micrograms.

items.t: Over 50 years (and elderly) without cardiac disease: start no more than 50 micrograms daily; increase by 50 micrograms every 3 to 4 weeks. Final dose 50 to 200 micrograms daily.

src.q: Initially, it is not advisable to exceed 50 micrograms daily. In this condition, the daily dose may be increased by 50 micrograms at intervals of every 3-4 weeks
Elderly Same as that for patients aged over 50 years.

items.t: Over 50 years with cardiac disease: 25 micrograms daily or 50 micrograms on alternate days; increase by 25 micrograms every 4 weeks. Final dose 50 to 200 micrograms daily. Clinical response is a better guide than serum levels over 50 years.

src.q: Where there is cardiac disease, 25 micrograms daily or 50 micrograms on alternate days is more suitable.
the daily dose may be increased by 25 micrograms at intervals of every 4 weeks

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: start 50 to 100 micrograms daily before breakfast; usual maintenance 100 to 200 micrograms daily. Adjust by 25 to 50 micrograms every 3 to 4 weeks.

src.q: Initial dose: 50 - 100 micrograms daily before breakfast. Usual maintenance dose: 100 - 200 micrograms daily.
The initial dose is adjusted by 25 to 50 microgram increments at 3 - 4 week intervals

items.t: Elderly, coronary heart disease, severe or long-standing hypothyroidism: low start (e.g. 12.5 micrograms/day), increase slowly (e.g. 12.5 micrograms/day every 2 weeks) with frequent thyroid monitoring.

src.q: a low initial dose (for example 12.5 microgram/day) should be given which should then be increased slowly and at lengthy intervals (e.g. a gradual increment of 12.5 microgram/day fortnightly) with frequent monitoring of thyroid hormones

items.t: Diffuse non-toxic goitre or Hashimoto's goitre: 50 to 200 µg/day. Stop if no decrease in goitre size after 6 to 12 months (non-toxic goitre with normal T4/TSH).

src.q: Diffuse non toxic goitre or goitre associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis The recommended dose is 50-200 µg/day.
If no discernible decrease in size of the goitre occurs after 6 to 12 month, thyroxine therapy should be stopped.

items.t: Suppression therapy in thyroid carcinoma: 150 to 300 µg/day.

src.q: Suppression therapy in thyroid carcinoma The recommended dose is 150-300 µg/day.

items.t: If metabolism rises too fast (diarrhoea, nervousness, fast pulse, insomnia, tremor, angina): reduce or withhold for 1 to 2 days, then restart at a lower dose.

src.q: reduce the dose or withhold for 1-2 days and start again at a lower dose

items.t: Neonates and infants with congenital hypothyroidism: 10 to 15 micrograms/kg/day for the first 3 months, then adjust to clinical findings, thyroid hormones and TSH.

src.q: the initial recommended dosage is 10 to 15 micrograms per kg BW per day for the first 3 months

items.t: Acquired hypothyroidism in children: start 12.5 to 50 micrograms/day; increase every 2 to 4 weeks by response and TSH until full replacement. Maintenance usually 100 to 150 micrograms/m² body surface area.

src.q: For children with acquired hypothyroidism, the initial recommended dosage is 12.5-50 micrograms per day.
The maintenance dose is generally 100 to 150 micrograms per m2 body surface area.

items.t: Juvenile myxoedema: start 25 micrograms daily; increase by 25 micrograms every 2 to 4 weeks until mild hyperthyroid symptoms, then reduce slightly.

src.q: Juvenile myxoedema in children: The initial recommended dosage is 25 micrograms daily.

items.t: Under 5 years: whole tablets not recommended, and crushing/dispersing tablets is not recommended (dosing inaccuracy); an approved oral solution is preferable.

src.q: In children under 5 years of age, the administration of whole tablets is not recommended.
In this age group it is preferable to administer an approved oral solution of levothyroxine.

items.t: Give infants the total daily dose at least 30 minutes before the first meal. Monitor TSH regularly. Very low birth weight preterm neonates: monitor haemodynamics at start (risk of circulatory collapse).

src.q: Infants should be given the total daily dose at least half an hour before the first meal of the day.
Haemodynamic parameters should be monitored when levothyroxine therapy is initiated in very low birth weight preterm neonates

items.t: Hypersensitivity to levothyroxine or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Tablet SmPC: thyrotoxicosis; adrenal gland disorder or adrenal insufficiency.

src.q: Thyrotoxicosis Adrenal gland disorder or adrenal insufficiency

items.t: Oral solution SmPC: adrenal insufficiency without adequate corticosteroid cover. (Thyrotoxicosis is not listed in this SmPC's 4.3; its 4.4 says do not give in hyperthyroid states except as supplementation during anti-thyroid treatment.)

src.q: In patients with adrenal insufficiency without adequate corticosteroid cover.
Levothyroxine should not be given in hyperthyreotic states other than as concomitant supplementation during anti-thyroid drug treatment of hyperthyroidism.

items.t: Must not be started in acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis or acute pancarditis (both SmPCs).

src.q: Treatment with Eltroxin must not be initiated in acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, and acute pancarditis.
Treatment with Levothyroxine Oral Solution must not be initiated in acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, and acute pancarditis.

items.t: Levothyroxine plus anti-thyroid drug for hyperthyroidism is not indicated in pregnancy.

src.q: Combination therapy of hyperthyroidism with levothyroxine and anti-thyroid agents is not indicated in pregnancy.

items.t: Start very gradually over 50 years and in long-standing hypothyroidism. Use with caution in cardiovascular disorders (angina, coronary artery disease, hypertension) and in the elderly; do an ECG before starting if cardiovascular disease is suspected or high risk, then start low and increase cautiously.

src.q: Levothyroxine should be introduced very gradually in patients aged over 50 years (see section 4.2) and those with long standing hypothyroidism
Levothyroxine sodium should be used with caution in patients with cardiovascular disorders, including angina, coronary artery disease, hypertension, and in the elderly
it is important to perform an ECG prior to commencement of levothyroxine treatment in order to detect changes consistent with ischaemia

items.t: Panhypopituitarism or adrenal insufficiency risk: start corticosteroid therapy before levothyroxine.

src.q: it is advisable to start corticosteroid therapy before giving levothyroxine to such patients

items.t: Over-treatment (low TSH) risks atrial fibrillation and fractures in older people: monitor TSH long term. Subclinical hyperthyroidism may cause bone loss; titrate to the lowest effective dose.

src.q: To minimise the risk of adverse effects of undetected overtreatment, such as atrial fibrillation and fractures associated with low serum levels of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) in older patients, it is important to monitor serum TSH
To minimise the risk of osteoporosis, dosage of levothyroxine sodium should be titrated to the lowest possible effective level.

items.t: Diabetes: may increase insulin/antidiabetic (e.g. metformin) requirements; care needed. Also care in diabetes insipidus.

src.q: Thyroid replacement therapy may cause an increase in dosage requirements of insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy (such as metformin). Care is needed for patients with diabetes mellitus, and diabetes insipidus.

items.t: Epilepsy: care required - seizures reported rarely on starting.

src.q: Care is required when levothyroxine is administered to patients with known history of epilepsy.

items.t: Switching products: a small number of patients report symptoms; consider thyroid function tests.

src.q: If patients report side effects on switching between products, consider thyroid function testing.

items.t: Biotin can interfere with thyroid immunoassays (falsely high or low results); tell the laboratory.

src.q: Biotin may interfere with thyroid immunoassays that are based on a biotin/streptavidin interaction, leading to either falsely decreased or falsely increased test results.

items.t: Tablets contain lactose (avoid in rare hereditary galactose intolerance, lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption). Oral solution contains parahydroxybenzoates and glycerol.

src.q: Lactose 48.86mg per tablet
This product contains: Parahydroxybenzoates. These may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed).

items.t: Warfarin/anticoagulants: effect increased; anticoagulant dose may need reducing to avoid bleeding.

src.q: Levothyroxine increases the effect of anticoagulants (Warfarin) and it may be necessary to reduce the anticoagulation dosage if excessive, hypoprothrombinaemia and bleeding are to be avoided.

items.t: Antidiabetic medicines (e.g. metformin): blood glucose rises; monitor for increased requirements.

src.q: A possible interaction occurs with hypoglycaemic agents, hence diabetic patients should be monitored for increased requirements of insulin or oral hypoglycaemic agents.

items.t: Antacids, calcium salts (e.g. calcium carbonate), oral iron (e.g. ferrous sulphate), aluminium hydroxide, sucralfate, colestyramine: reduce absorption - separate doses (tablet SmPC: by 4 to 5 hours; oral solution SmPC: by several hours).

src.q: Absorption of levothyroxine (thyroxine) possibly reduced by antacids, calcium salts, cimetidine, oral iron, sucralfate, colestipol, polystyrene sulphonate resin and cholestyramine (administration should be separated by 4-5 hours).
Cimetidine, aluminium hydroxide, calcium carbonate and ferrous sulphate also reduce absorption of levothyroxine from the G.I. tract. Dosages should be separated by an interval of several hours.

items.t: Proton pump inhibitors: may reduce absorption - monitor thyroid function during co-treatment and when the PPI stops; dose may need increasing.

src.q: Regular monitoring of thyroid function and clinical monitoring is recommended during concomitant treatment. It may be necessary to increase the dose of thyroid hormones. Care should also be taken when treatment with PPI ends.

items.t: St John's wort, rifampicin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, phenytoin: increase levothyroxine metabolism - dose may need increasing.

src.q: Metabolism of levothyroxine (thyroxine) is accelerated by rifampicin, barbituarates, products containing St John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum L.) and primidone.

items.t: Sertraline: may reduce the effect of levothyroxine.

src.q: Effects of Levothyroxine may be decreased by concomitant sertraline.

items.t: Orlistat: may reduce absorption (monitor thyroid function). Ritonavir: monitor TSH for at least the first month after starting/stopping. Oestrogens/oral contraceptives may increase requirements. Amiodarone, lithium, tyrosine kinase inhibitors and others can affect thyroid function.

src.q: Anti-obesity drugs such as orlistat may decrease levothyroxine absorption which may result in hypothyroidism (monitor for changes in thyroid function).
Thyroid- stimulating hormone (TSH) should be monitored in patients treated with levothyroxine at least the first month after starting and /or ending ritonavir treatment.
Oestrogen, oestrogen containing product (including hormone replacement therapy) and oral contraceptives may increase the requirement of thyroid therapy dosage.

items.t: Tricyclic antidepressants, sympathomimetics: effects enhanced (arrhythmia risk). Digoxin dose may need adjusting. Aspirin/NSAIDs can give falsely low plasma thyroid hormone concentrations.

src.q: concomitant use may precipitate cardiac arrhythmias
If levothyroxine therapy is initiated in digitalised patients, the dose of digitalis may require adjustment.
False low plasma concentrations have been observed with concurrent anti-inflammatory treatment such as phenylbutazone or acetylsalicylic acid and levothyroxine therapy.

renal.note: No renal impairment dose advice in the tablet or oral solution SmPCs accessed.

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment dose advice in the tablet or oral solution SmPCs accessed.

items.t: Tablet SmPC: safety in pregnancy not known; weigh any possible risk against the risk to the fetus of untreated hypothyroidism.

src.q: The safety of Levothyroxine treatment during pregnancy is not known, but any possible risk of foetal abnormalities should be weighed against the risk to the foetus of untreated hypothyroidism.

items.t: Oral solution SmPC: continue treatment consistently in pregnancy; monitor closely - dose requirements may increase. No evidence of teratogenicity at therapeutic doses; avoid excessive doses.

src.q: Women on a maintenance dose for hypothyroidism who become pregnant, must be monitored closely.
Treatment with levothyroxine should be given consistently during pregnancy and breast-feeding in particular. Dosage requirements may even increase during pregnancy.

items.t: Levothyroxine with anti-thyroid drugs for hyperthyroidism is not indicated in pregnancy (anti-thyroid drugs cross the placenta).

src.q: Such combination would require higher doses of anti-thyroid agents, which are known to pass the placenta and to induce hypothyroidism in the infant.

items.t: SPS: consider referring pregnant or post-partum patients with hypothyroidism.

src.q: Consider referring patients with hypothyroidism who
are pregnant or post-partum

items.t: Oral solution SmPC: passes into milk but not enough to cause hyperthyroidism or TSH suppression in the infant; can be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: Levothyroxine can be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: Tablet SmPC: excreted in milk in low concentrations; it is debated whether this can interfere with neonatal screening.

src.q: Levothyroxine is excreted in breast milk in low concentrations, and it is contentious whether this can interfere with neonatal screening.

items.t: Fertility: no data. Oestrogen-containing contraceptives/HRT may increase levothyroxine requirements.

src.q: Fertility No data available
Oestrogen, oestrogen containing product (including hormone replacement therapy) and oral contraceptives may increase the requirement of thyroid therapy dosage.

items.t: Frequency not known. Side effects usually mean the dose is too high (hyperthyroid symptoms): palpitations, tachycardia, arrhythmia, angina, tremor, restlessness, insomnia, diarrhoea, vomiting, sweating, flushing, weight loss, headache, irregular periods. They usually settle on dose reduction.

src.q: Side-effects are usually indicative of excessive dosage and usually disappear on reduction of dosage or withdrawal of treatment for a few days.
Cardiac disorders Angina pectoris, arrhythmia, palpitations, tachycardia

items.t: Children: transient hair loss in the first months is common and usually regrows.

src.q: partial loss of hair may occur during the first few months of therapy, but this effect is usually transient

items.t: Thyrotoxic crisis (high fever, tachycardia, arrhythmia, hypotension, heart failure, jaundice, confusion, seizures, coma): urgent medical care.

src.q: This is called a "thyroid crisis" with any of the following symptoms: Hyperpyrexia, tachycardia, arrhythmia, hypotension, cardiac failure, jaundice, confusion, seizure and coma

items.t: Angina or worsening ischaemia (latent cardiac ischaemia) if the dose rises too fast: reduce or withhold, then restart lower.

src.q: dosage must be reduced, or withheld, for a day or two, and then re-started at a lower dose level

items.t: Children: benign intracranial hypertension, craniostenosis in infants, premature closure of epiphyses.

src.q: Heat intolerance, transient hair loss, benign intracranial hypertension, craniostenosis in infants and premature closure of epiphysis in children.

items.t: Before starting: TSH, free T4 (thyroid function tests) and ECG (SPS); ECG especially if cardiovascular disease is suspected (SmPC).

src.q: Before starting Required Baseline ECG Free T4 Thyroid function tests Thyroid stimulating hormone
A pre-therapy ECG is valuable because ECG changes due to hypothyroidism may be confused with ECG evidence of cardiac ischaemia.

items.t: After starting or a dose change: TSH from 6 weeks, repeated every 3 months (free T4 if symptoms continue). Adjust dose about every 4 weeks by 25 to 50 micrograms (25 micrograms in higher-risk patients: over 65, cardiac disease, severe hypothyroidism, thyroid cancer, adrenal insufficiency, pregnancy).

src.q: From 6 weeks; repeated every 3 months Thyroid stimulating hormone
For patients without risk factors, adjust doses every 4 weeks in increments of 25-50 micrograms according to response.
For these patients adjust doses cautiously, for example, every 4 weeks in increments of 25 micrograms according to response.

items.t: Once stable (2 similar in-range results 3 months apart): TSH annually.

src.q: Patients who record 2 similar measurements within the reference range 3 months apart should be considered for ongoing once stable monitoring.
Ongoing once stable Required Annually Thyroid stimulating hormone

items.t: Thyroid function during and after interacting medicines (PPIs: during co-treatment and when the PPI stops; orlistat; ritonavir: TSH for at least the first month after starting or stopping) and after switching products if symptomatic.

src.q: Regular monitoring of thyroid function and clinical monitoring is recommended during concomitant treatment. It may be necessary to increase the dose of thyroid hormones. Care should also be taken when treatment with PPI ends.
Anti-obesity drugs such as orlistat may decrease levothyroxine absorption which may result in hypothyroidism (monitor for changes in thyroid function).
Thyroid- stimulating hormone (TSH) should be monitored in patients treated with levothyroxine at least the first month after starting and /or ending ritonavir treatment.
if a patient reports symptoms after changing their levothyroxine product, consider testing thyroid function

items.t: If signs of too-rapid increase in metabolism: reduce or withhold for 1 to 2 days, restart lower.

src.q: reduce the dose or withhold for 1-2 days and start again at a lower dose

items.t: Take once daily on an empty stomach, usually before breakfast.

src.q: Levothyroxine is best taken as a single dose on an empty stomach, usually before breakfast.
preferably taken before breakfast or the first meal of the day

items.t: Separate from antacids, calcium, iron and similar products by several hours (tablet SmPC: 4 to 5 hours).

src.q: (administration should be separated by 4-5 hours)

items.t: Usually lifelong treatment for hypothyroidism. Do not use for weight loss.

src.q: Duration of treatment is usually for life in the case of hypothyroidism
Thyroid hormones are not suitable for weight reduction.

items.t: Report palpitations, chest pain, tremor, sleeplessness or diarrhoea (dose may be too high).

src.q: causing diarrhoea, nervousness, rapid pulse, insomnia, tremors, and sometimes anginal pain where there is latent cardiac ischaemia

items.t: Report symptoms after a change of product to your prescriber.

src.q: report suspected adverse reactions to levothyroxine medicines, including symptoms after switching products, to the Yellow Card scheme

items.t: Tell the laboratory if you take biotin supplements before thyroid blood tests.

src.q: For patients taking biotin-containing products, laboratory personnel should be informed when a thyroid function test is requested.
Each tablet contains lisinopril dihydrate equivalent to 5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg anhydrous lisinopril.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Hypertension; symptomatic heart failure; short-term (6 weeks) treatment of haemodynamically stable patients within 24 hours of acute myocardial infarction; renal disease in hypertensive patients with type 2 diabetes and incipient nephropathy.

src.q: Hypertension Treatment of hypertension. Heart failure Treatment of symptomatic heart failure.
Short-term (6 weeks) treatment of haemodynamically stable patients within 24 hours of an acute myocardial infarction.
Treatment of renal disease in hypertensive patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and incipient nephropathy

restrictions.note: No specialist-only or shared-care restriction stated in the lisinopril SmPC. Dual RAAS blockade, if absolutely necessary, only under specialist supervision (see cautions).

items.t: Usual starting dose 10 mg once daily. Usual maintenance 20 mg once daily; increase if needed after 2-4 weeks at a dose. Maximum used in long-term trials: 80 mg/day.

src.q: In patients with hypertension the usual recommended starting dose is 10 mg.
The usual effective maintenance dosage is 20 mg administered in a single daily dose.
if the desired therapeutic effect cannot be achieved in a period of 2 to 4 weeks on a certain dose level, the dose can be further increased.
The maximum dose used in long-term, controlled clinical trials was 80 mg/day.

items.t: Strongly activated renin-angiotensin system (renovascular hypertension, salt/volume depletion, cardiac decompensation, severe hypertension): start 2.5-5 mg under medical supervision.

src.q: A starting dose of 2.5-5 mg is recommended in such patients and the initiation of treatment should take place under medical supervision.

items.t: Already on a diuretic: if possible stop the diuretic 2-3 days before starting; if it cannot be stopped, start at 5 mg. Monitor renal function and serum potassium.

src.q: If possible, the diuretic should be discontinued 2 to 3 days before beginning therapy with Zestril.
In hypertensive patients in whom the diuretic cannot be discontinued, therapy with Zestril should be initiated with a 5 mg dose. Renal function and serum potassium should be monitored.

items.t: Start 2.5 mg once daily under medical supervision. Increase in steps of no more than 10 mg, at intervals of at least 2 weeks, to the highest tolerated dose, maximum 35 mg once daily.

src.q: Zestril may be initiated at a starting dose of 2.5 mg once a day, which should be administered under medical supervision to determine the initial effect on the blood pressure.
By increments of no greater than 10 mg At intervals of no less than 2 weeks To the highest dose tolerated by the patient up to a maximum of 35 mg once daily.

items.t: Start within 24 hours of symptoms only if systolic BP is at least 100 mmHg: 5 mg, then 5 mg after 24 hours, 10 mg after 48 hours, then 10 mg once daily for 6 weeks, then re-evaluate. Systolic BP 120 mmHg or lower in the first 3 days: 2.5 mg. Maintenance: reduce to 5 mg (temporarily 2.5 mg) if systolic BP 100 mmHg or lower; withdraw if systolic BP below 90 mmHg for more than 1 hour.

src.q: Treatment should not be started if systolic blood pressure is lower than 100 mm Hg.
The first dose of Zestril is 5 mg given orally, followed by 5 mg after 24 hours, 10 mg after 48 hours and then 10 mg once daily.
should be given a lower dose - 2.5 mg orally
If prolonged hypotension occurs (systolic blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg for more than 1 hour) Zestril should be withdrawn.
Treatment should continue for 6 weeks and then the patient should be re-evaluated.

items.t: 10 mg once daily, increased to 20 mg once daily if needed to reach a sitting diastolic BP below 90 mmHg.

src.q: the dose is 10 mg Zestril once daily which can be increased to 20 mg once daily, if necessary, to achieve a sitting diastolic blood pressure below 90 mm Hg.

items.t: Elderly: use the renal table (CrCl) for the starting dose when age is linked with reduced renal function, then adjust to blood pressure.

src.q: When advanced age is associated with decrease in renal function, however, the guidelines set out in Table 1 should be used to determine the starting dose of Zestril.

items.t: Hypertension, 6-16 years: 20 to under 50 kg, start 2.5 mg once daily, maximum 20 mg daily; 50 kg or more, start 5 mg once daily, maximum 40 mg daily. Doses above 0.61 mg/kg (or above 40 mg) not studied.

src.q: The recommended initial dose is 2.5 mg once daily in patients 20 to <50 kg, and 5 mg once daily in patients ≥50 kg.
The dosage should be individually adjusted to a maximum of 20 mg daily in patients weighing 20 to <50 kg, and 40 mg in patients ≥50 kg.
Doses above 0.61 mg/kg (or in excess of 40 mg) have not been studied in paediatric patients

items.t: Not recommended under 6 years, in children with severe renal impairment (GFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²), or for indications other than hypertension. Consider a lower starting dose or longer interval in children with reduced renal function.

src.q: Zestril is not recommended in children below the age of 6, or in children with severe renal impairment (GFR < 30ml/min/1.73m2)
Zestril is not recommended in children in other indications than hypertension.
In children with decreased renal function, a lower starting dose or increased dosing interval should be considered.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to lisinopril, any excipient or any other ACE inhibitor.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to Zestril, to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 or any other angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor.

items.t: History of angioedema with previous ACE inhibitor therapy; hereditary or idiopathic angioedema.

src.q: History of angioedema associated with previous ACE inhibitor therapy.
Hereditary or idiopathic angioedema.

items.t: With sacubitril/valsartan; do not start lisinopril within 36 hours of the last sacubitril/valsartan dose.

src.q: Zestril must not be initiated earlier than 36 hours after the last dose of sacubitril/valsartan

items.t: Second and third trimesters of pregnancy.

src.q: Second and third trimesters of pregnancy (see sections 4.4 and 4.6).

items.t: With aliskiren-containing products in patients with diabetes or renal impairment (GFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m²).

src.q: The concomitant use of Zestril with aliskiren-containing products is contraindicated in patients with diabetes mellitus or renal impairment (GFR < 60 ml/min/1.73 m2)

items.t: Symptomatic hypotension: more likely with volume depletion (diuretics, salt restriction, dialysis, diarrhoea, vomiting), severe renin-dependent hypertension or heart failure. Monitor starting and dose changes closely in those at risk, including ischaemic heart or cerebrovascular disease.

src.q: hypotension is more likely to occur if the patient has been volume-depleted, e.g. by diuretic therapy, dietary salt restriction, dialysis, diarrhoea or vomiting, or has severe renin-dependent hypertension
In patients at increased risk of symptomatic hypotension, initiation of therapy and dose adjustment should be closely monitored.

items.t: Acute MI: must not be started if systolic BP 100 mmHg or lower or in cardiogenic shock. Do not start with renal dysfunction (serum creatinine above 177 micromol/l and/or proteinuria above 500 mg/24 h); consider withdrawal if creatinine rises above 265 micromol/l or doubles.

src.q: These are patients with systolic blood pressure of 100 mm Hg or lower, or those in cardiogenic shock.

treatment with Zestril should not be initiated in patients with evidence of renal dysfunction, defined as serum creatinine concentration exceeding 177 micromol/l and/or proteinuria exceeding 500 mg/24 h.
(serum creatinine concentration exceeding 265 micromol/l or a doubling from the pre-treatment value) then the physician should consider withdrawal of Zestril.

items.t: Mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: give with caution.

src.q: Zestril should be given with caution to patients with mitral valve stenosis and obstruction in the outflow of the left ventricle such as aortic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

items.t: Bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis to a single kidney: urea and creatinine may rise; start under close supervision with low doses and careful titration.

src.q: In these patients, treatment should be started under close medical supervision with low doses and careful dose titration.

items.t: Angioedema can occur at any time, including after months or years of treatment. Stop promptly; standard treatments for histamine-mediated angioedema may not work for bradykinin-mediated angioedema. Higher rate in black patients.

src.q: severe angioedema may also develop after months or years of long-term treatment with an ACE inhibitor. In such cases, Zestril should be discontinued promptly
standard therapies for histamine-mediated angioedema may be ineffective for bradykinin-mediated angioedema

items.t: History of angioedema not caused by an ACE inhibitor: may be at higher risk of angioedema on an ACE inhibitor (hereditary or idiopathic angioedema is a contraindication).

src.q: Patients with a history of angioedema unrelated to ACE inhibitor therapy may be at increased risk of angioedema while receiving an ACE inhibitor

items.t: Neutropenia/agranulocytosis: extreme caution in collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, allopurinol or procainamide, especially with renal impairment; check white cell counts periodically.

src.q: Zestril should be used with extreme caution in patients with collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, treatment with allopurinol or procainamide
periodic monitoring of white blood cell counts is advised

items.t: Hyperkalaemia risk with renal impairment, diabetes, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, potassium-sparing diuretics, trimethoprim/co-trimoxazole, aldosterone antagonists or ARBs. Monitor potassium and renal function.

src.q: Potassium-sparing diuretics and angiotensin-receptor blockers should be used with caution in patients receiving ACE inhibitors, and serum potassium and renal function should be monitored

items.t: Dual RAAS blockade (ACE inhibitor with ARB or aliskiren) not recommended; if absolutely necessary only under specialist supervision with close monitoring. Do not combine an ACE inhibitor and ARB in diabetic nephropathy.

src.q: Dual blockade of RAAS through the combined use of ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers or aliskiren is therefore not recommended
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers should not be used concomitantly in patients with diabetic nephropathy.

items.t: Diabetes on insulin or oral antidiabetics: monitor glycaemic control closely in the first month.

src.q: glycaemic control should be closely monitored during the first month of treatment with an ACE inhibitor

items.t: Hepatic failure (very rare): stop if jaundice or marked rise in liver enzymes.

src.q: Patients receiving Zestril who develop jaundice or marked elevations of hepatic enzymes should discontinue Zestril and receive appropriate medical follow-up.

items.t: Persistent dry cough can occur and resolves after stopping.

src.q: Characteristically, the cough is non-productive, persistent and resolves after discontinuation of therapy.

items.t: Major surgery or anaesthesia: hypotension can occur; correct with volume expansion.

src.q: If hypotension occurs and is considered to be due to this mechanism, it can be corrected by volume expansion.

items.t: Anaphylactoid reactions with high-flux dialysis membranes (e.g. AN 69), LDL apheresis with dextran sulphate, and desensitisation (e.g. venom).

src.q: Anaphylactoid reactions have been reported in patients dialysed with high flux membranes (e.g. AN 69) and treated concomitantly with an ACE inhibitor.

items.t: Recent kidney transplant: no experience; not recommended.

src.q: There is no experience regarding the administration of Zestril in patients with recent kidney transplantation. Treatment with Zestril is therefore not recommended.

items.t: Potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone), potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, trimethoprim and co-trimoxazole: risk of significant hyperkalaemia, especially with renal impairment. Combination not recommended; if needed, use with caution and monitor potassium frequently.

src.q: Use of potassium sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene or amiloride), potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes, particularly in patients with impaired renal function, may lead to a significant increase in serum potassium.

Therefore, the combination of Zestril with the above-mentioned drugs is not recommended. If concomitant use is indicated, they should be used with caution and with frequent monitoring of serum potassium.

items.t: NSAIDs (including aspirin at anti-inflammatory doses): reduced antihypertensive effect; risk of worsening renal function, including acute renal failure, and raised potassium. Use with caution (especially in the elderly), keep hydrated and consider monitoring renal function.

src.q: Concomitant use of ACE inhibitors and NSAIDs may lead to an increased risk of worsening of renal function, including possible acute renal failure, and an increase in serum potassium
The combination should be administered with caution, especially in the elderly.

items.t: Antidiabetic medicines (insulin, oral agents): greater glucose lowering with risk of hypoglycaemia, mostly in the first weeks and in renal impairment.

src.q: may cause an increased blood glucose-lowering effect with risk of hypoglycaemia

items.t: Diuretics: additive effect; excessive BP fall when lisinopril is added, especially if the diuretic was started recently.

src.q: Patients already on diuretics and especially those in whom diuretic therapy was recently instituted, may occasionally experience an excessive reduction of blood pressure when Zestril is added.

items.t: Nitrates and other antihypertensives/vasodilators: additive falls in blood pressure. Lisinopril may be used with nitrates, aspirin at cardiac doses, thrombolytics and beta-blockers.

src.q: When Zestril is combined with other antihypertensive agents (e.g. glyceryl trinitrate and other nitrates, or other vasodilators), additive falls in blood pressure may occur.
Zestril may be used concomitantly with acetylsalicylic acid (at cardiologic doses), thrombolytics, beta-blockers and/or nitrates.

items.t: Sacubitril/valsartan: contraindicated (angioedema). mTOR inhibitors, racecadotril, vildagliptin, tissue plasminogen activator: higher angioedema risk.

src.q: Concomitant use of ACE inhibitors with sacubitril/valsartan is contraindicated as this increases the risk of angioedema

items.t: Lithium: not recommended; if needed, monitor lithium levels carefully. Ciclosporin or heparin: monitor potassium.

src.q: Use of Zestril with lithium is not recommended, but if the combination proves necessary, careful monitoring of serum lithium levels should be performed
Hyperkalaemia may occur during concomitant use of ACE inhibitors with ciclosporin. Monitoring of serum potassium is recommended.

items.t: Starting dose by creatinine clearance: below 10 mL/min (including dialysis) 2.5 mg; 10-30 mL/min 2.5-5 mg; 31-80 mL/min 5-10 mg. Then titrate to blood pressure up to a maximum of 40 mg daily.

src.q: Dosage in patients with renal impairment should be based on creatinine clearance as outlined in Table 1 below.
Less than 10 ml/min (including patients on dialysis) 2.5 mg* 10-30 ml/min 2.5-5 mg 31-80 ml/min 5-10 mg
The dosage may be titrated upward until blood pressure is controlled or to a maximum of 40 mg daily.

items.t: Heart failure, MI and diabetic nephropathy: adjust the initial dose to creatinine clearance when below 80 mL/min.

src.q: In cases of renal impairment (creatinine clearance <80 ml/min), the initial Zestril dosage should be adjusted according to the patient's creatinine clearance (see Table 1).

items.t: SPS: seek specialist advice before starting if eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m².

src.q: eGFR less than 30ml/min/1.73m2
Seek specialist advice prior to initiation for patients where there is:

items.t: SPS: some rise in creatinine is expected. Acceptable: creatinine rise under 50% above baseline (if below 266 micromol/L) or eGFR fall under 10% (if eGFR over 25). In CKD: eGFR fall over 25% or creatinine rise over 30% - look for other causes (e.g. volume depletion, NSAIDs); if none, stop or reduce to the previously tolerated dose.

src.q: An increase in serum creatinine of less than 50% above baseline, as long as it is less than 266 micromol/L, or a decrease in eGFR of less than 10% from baseline, as long as eGFR is over 25 mL/min/1.73 m2, can be considered as acceptable.
If no alternative cause is identified: Stop ACEI/ARB or reduce to previously tolerated dose

items.t: No hepatic dose adjustment stated. In cirrhosis, absorption fell about 30% but exposure rose about 50% (lower clearance).

src.q: Impairment of hepatic function in cirrhotic patients resulted in a decrease in lisinopril absorption (about 30% as determined by urinary recovery), but an increase in exposure (approximately 50%) compared to healthy subjects due to decreased clearance.

items.t: Very rarely ACE inhibitors cause cholestatic jaundice progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis; stop lisinopril if jaundice or marked liver enzyme rise.

src.q: Very rarely, ACE inhibitors have been associated with a syndrome that starts with cholestatic jaundice and progresses to fulminant necrosis and (sometimes) death.
Patients receiving Zestril who develop jaundice or marked elevations of hepatic enzymes should discontinue Zestril

items.t: SmPC: not recommended in the first trimester; contraindicated in the second and third trimesters. Stop as soon as pregnancy is diagnosed and switch if appropriate. If exposed from the second trimester, ultrasound check of fetal renal function and skull; watch the newborn for hypotension.

src.q: The use of ACE inhibitors is not recommended during the first trimester of pregnancy
The use of ACE inhibitors is contra-indicated during the second and third trimester of pregnancy
When pregnancy is diagnosed, treatment with ACE inhibitors should be stopped immediately, and, if appropriate, alternative therapy should be started.
Should exposure to ACE inhibitors have occurred from the second trimester of pregnancy, ultrasound check of renal function and skull is recommended.

items.t: MHRA: ACE inhibitors should not be used at any stage of pregnancy unless absolutely necessary, and only after discussing risks and benefits. On diagnosis of pregnancy, stop as soon as possible.

src.q: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor antagonists should not be used at any stage of pregnancy unless absolutely necessary
On diagnosis of pregnancy, treatment with an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist should be stopped as soon as possible

items.t: BUMPS: early-pregnancy use is unlikely to harm the baby; use after about 20 weeks can cause oligohydramnios, fetal kidney damage, skull under-development, growth restriction, lung under-development and joint contractures, and may raise stillbirth risk. Extra monitoring is needed if continued after about 20 weeks.

src.q: Taking an ACE-I in early pregnancy is unlikely to harm your baby.
Taking an ACE-I after around 20 weeks of pregnancy can cause a number of problems in your baby
If you continue to take an ACE-I after around 20 weeks you will require additional monitoring to assess amniotic fluid levels and your baby's growth and wellbeing.

items.t: SmPC: no information; not recommended. Alternatives with better established safety are preferable, especially with a newborn or preterm infant.

src.q: Because no information is available regarding the use of Zestril during breast-feeding, Zestril is not recommended

items.t: MHRA (2009): lisinopril not recommended in breastfeeding; prefer alternatives, especially with a newborn or preterm baby. Clarification: not recommended but not absolutely contraindicated; may be prescribed if essential for the mother.

src.q: ramipril, lisinopril, fosinopril, trandolapril, moexipril, or perindopril: use in breastfeeding is not recommended
they are not absolutely contraindicated. Healthcare professionals may prescribe these medicines during breastfeeding if they consider that this treatment is essential for the lactating mother.

items.t: SPS (2023): lisinopril can be used with caution; enalapril is the preferred ACE inhibitor. Watch the infant for hypotension (drowsiness, lethargy, pallor, poor feeding, poor weight gain) and, in younger infants, for normal wet nappies. Neonates and infants under 2 months are at most risk.

src.q: Lisinopril can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but enalapril is preferred.
In younger infants, monitor for normal urine production (wet nappies).
Neonates and infants less than 2 months are at the most risk from the side-effects of ACE inhibitors, particularly hypotension

items.t: Planning pregnancy: switch to an antihypertensive with an established pregnancy safety profile unless continued ACE inhibitor treatment is essential.

src.q: Unless continued ACE inhibitor therapy is considered essential, patients planning pregnancy should be changed to alternative anti-hypertensive treatments which have an established safety profile for use in pregnancy.

items.t: Common: dizziness, headache, orthostatic effects (including hypotension), cough, diarrhoea, vomiting, renal dysfunction.

src.q: common: dizziness, headache
common: orthostatic effects (including hypotension)
common: cough
common: diarrhoea, vomiting
common: renal dysfunction

items.t: Angioedema (face, lips, tongue, glottis, larynx; also intestinal): can occur at any time, even after years. Stop the ACE inhibitor at once and do not restart. Bradykinin-mediated angioedema may not respond to adrenaline; lack of response should prompt this diagnosis. Airway involvement needs emergency treatment.

src.q: if angioedema is suspected in a patient taking an ACE inhibitor, discontinue the ACE inhibitor immediately and do not restart
bradykinin-mediated angioedema is unlikely to respond to standard anaphylaxis treatments including adrenaline (epinephrine)
Patients with involvement of the tongue, glottis or larynx, are likely to experience airway obstruction

items.t: Hyperkalaemia (uncommon); acute renal failure (rare); hyponatraemia (rare).

src.q: uncommon: increases in blood urea, increases in serum creatinine, increases in liver enzymes, hyperkalaemia
rare: uraemia, acute renal failure

items.t: Very rare: bone marrow depression, agranulocytosis, neutropenia; pancreatitis; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic failure; Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis.

src.q: very rare: bone marrow depression, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, neutropenia, agranulocytosis
very rare: pancreatitis, intestinal angioedema, hepatitis - either hepatocellular or cholestatic, jaundice and hepatic failure
toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome

items.t: SPS baseline: blood pressure, eGFR or serum creatinine, serum potassium, serum sodium. Starting is not normally appropriate if potassium is above 5.0 mmol/L.

src.q: Baseline Blood pressure Estimated glomerular filtration rate or Serum creatinine (for creatinine clearance) Serum potassium Serum sodium
Initiation not normally appropriate if pre-treatment potassium greater than 5.0mmol/L

items.t: SPS: seek specialist advice before starting in severe or unstable heart failure, renovascular disease, eGFR below 30, sodium below 130 mmol/L, hypovolaemia, systolic BP below 90 mmHg, multiple or high-dose diuretics (furosemide 80 mg daily or more), high-dose vasodilator, significant valve disease.

src.q: Seek specialist advice prior to initiation for patients where there is: severe or unstable heart failure renovascular disease eGFR less than 30ml/min/1.73m2 hyponatraemia (sodium less than 130mmol/L) hypovolaemia hypotension (systolic blood pressure less than 90mmHg)

items.t: SPS after starting or a dose change: heart failure - renal function, sodium and potassium within 1-2 weeks (5-7 days with other risk factors), BP before and after each dose change; hypertension - renal function, sodium, potassium within 1-2 weeks (7 days with risk factors), BP within 1 month; post-MI - BP, renal function, sodium, potassium within 1-2 weeks.

src.q: Heart failure with other risk factors Within 5 - 7 days
Hypertension Within 1 - 2 weeks Estimated glomerular filtration rate or Serum creatinine (for creatinine clearance) Serum sodium Serum potassium Within 1 month Blood pressure

items.t: SPS once stable: heart failure every 3-6 months (renal function, sodium, potassium); hypertension and post-MI annually. Repeat at any time if acutely unwell.

src.q: Ongoing once stable Heart failure Every 3 - 6 months
Hypertension Annually Serum sodium Serum potassium
Repeat monitoring at any time patient acutely unwell or their renal function may be compromised.

items.t: SPS abnormal results: potassium above 5.5 mmol/L - follow local guidance; potassium 6.0 mmol/L or above in CKD - stop the ACE inhibitor (after stopping other potassium-raising drugs) and seek specialist advice; sodium below 132 mmol/L - specialist advice.

src.q: Value 6.0 mmol/L or above in people with CKD Stop ACEI/ARB after stopping other drugs that may increase potassium and seek specialist advice.
Sodium Value is below 132mmol/L Obtain specialist advice

items.t: Acute MI: withdraw if systolic BP below 90 mmHg for more than 1 hour; consider withdrawal if creatinine exceeds 265 micromol/l or doubles.

src.q: If hypotension persists (systolic blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg for more than 1 hour) then Zestril should be withdrawn.

items.t: Once daily at about the same time each day; food does not affect absorption.

src.q: Zestril should be taken at approximately the same time each day. The absorption of Zestril tablets is not affected by food.

items.t: Seek urgent help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or trouble breathing or swallowing, even after long use; do not take further doses. Tell staff about any past angioedema.

src.q: seek urgent medical attention if you develop swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or experience difficulty breathing or swallowing whilst taking ACE inhibitors
do not take further doses of your ACE inhibitor if angioedema is suspected and inform a healthcare professional immediately

items.t: Planning pregnancy or pregnant: contact the doctor to switch medicine.

src.q: If you find out that you are pregnant whilst taking an ACE-I, you should contact your doctor as soon as possible so that you can be switched to another medicine.

items.t: Dizziness or tiredness can affect driving.

src.q: When driving vehicles or operating machines it should be taken into account that occasionally dizziness or tiredness may occur.

items.t: Avoid potassium salt substitutes unless advised (risk of high potassium).

src.q: potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes, particularly in patients with impaired renal function, may lead to a significant increase in serum potassium.

formulations.label: Chewable tablets 4 mmol
formulations.strengths: Magnesium glycerophosphate equivalent to 4 mmol (97.2 mg) magnesium per tablet
formulations.note: Contains aspartame (10 mg per tablet) and phosphate. The score line is for ease of swallowing, not for dividing into equal doses.

src.q: Each chewable tablet contains magnesium glycerophosphate equivalent to 4 mmol (97.2 mg) of magnesium.
Each tablet contains 10 mg aspartame.
The score line is only to facilitate breaking for ease of swallowing and not to divide into equal doses.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Chronic magnesium loss or hypomagnesaemia diagnosed by a doctor.

src.q: indicated as oral magnesium supplements for the treatment of patients with chronic magnesium loss or hypomagnesaemia as diagnosed by a doctor

items.t: Adults with hypomagnesaemia caused by loop or thiazide diuretics or other drugs that cause hypomagnesaemia.

src.q: also indicated for adult patients with hypomagnesaemia due to the concomitant administration of loop and thiazide diuretics or other drugs which cause hypomagnesaemia

items.t: Children: use only if benefits outweigh risks and under supervision of physicians experienced in managing hypomagnesaemia in children.

src.q: Neomag tablets should only be used if the benefits of treatment outweigh any potential risks and under the supervision of physicians experienced in the management of children with hypomagnesaemia.

items.t: Severe symptomatic hypomagnesaemia: give IV magnesium first to restore levels, before oral magnesium glycerophosphate.

src.q: Patients with severe, symptomatic hypomagnesaemia should receive intravenous magnesium repletion for acute recovery of magnesium levels prior to receiving Neomag.

items.t: Adults (over 18 years): start 4-8 mmol (1-2 tablets) three times a day (12-24 mmol/day in divided doses); adjust to serum total magnesium. Elderly: no dose adjustment.

src.q: Starting doses for adult patients are recommended as 4-8 mmol (1-2 tablets) administered 3 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 12 to 24 mmol per day taken in divided doses.
Elderly: No dose adjustment is necessary.

items.t: SPS (mild hypomagnesaemia, 0.5-0.7 mmol/L): total daily oral dose 10-24 mmol magnesium in divided doses. Commonly given for up to 7 days, then recheck serum magnesium; continue 1-2 days after levels normalise.
items.tag: SPS: mild acute hypomagnesaemia in adults

src.q: Give a total daily oral dose of 10 to 24mmol of magnesium in divided doses.
It is common practice to prescribe oral magnesium replacement for up to 7 days and then repeat the serum magnesium level.
Continue treatment for 1 to 2 days after magnesium levels normalise.

items.t: Start low (e.g. 1 tablet per dose) and increase gradually to the maximum tolerated dose.

src.q: Start with a low dose, such as 1 tablet per dose, and gradually increase to a maximum tolerated dose.

items.t: Under 4 years: not recommended (insufficient information).

src.q: Children: below 4 years : Not recommended as there is insufficient information regarding the use of Neomag tablets in this age group.

items.t: 4 to 12 years: start 4 mmol (1 tablet) twice a day (8 mmol/day); adjust to serum total magnesium.

src.q: A starting dose for children 4 to 12 years is recommended as 4 mmol (1 tablet) administered 2 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 8 mmol per day taken in divided doses.

items.t: 12 to 18 years: start 4 mmol (1 tablet) three times a day (12 mmol/day); adjust to serum total magnesium.

src.q: A starting dose for children 12 to 18 years is recommended as 4 mmol (1 tablet) administered 3 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 12 mmol per day taken in divided doses.

items.t: Use only under supervision of physicians experienced in childhood hypomagnesaemia; monitor serum magnesium regularly.

src.q: under the supervision of physicians experienced in the management of children with hypomagnesaemia

items.t: Hypersensitivity to magnesium glycerophosphate or any excipient.

src.q: Do not administer Neomag tablets if there is evidence of hypersensitivity to the active substance

items.t: Severe renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate < 30 ml/min).

src.q: Neomag is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (glomerularfiltration rate < 30 ml/min).

items.t: Should not be given in phenylketonuria (contains aspartame) or hyperphosphataemia (contains phosphate). Both are listed in SmPC 4.3.

src.q: Neomag should not be administered to patients with phenylketonuria as Neomag tablets contain Aspartame.
Neomag should not be administered to patients with hyperphosphataemia as Neomag tablets contain phosphate.

items.t: Absorption may be reduced after extensive bowel resection.

magnesium preparations should be taken 3 to 4 hours before or after the administration of those drugs

src.q: multivalent cation-containing drugs and mineral supplements (e.g. calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron)

proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole and pantoprazole)

long-term data available from treatment of pre-eclampsia do not indicate malformative or feto/neonatal toxicity of magnesium

src.q: Neomag can be used during breast-feeding.
at therapeutic doses of Neomag no effects on the breastfed newborns/infants are anticipated

items.t: No effects on male or female fertility are expected.

concomitant hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia should be suspected and corrected if confirmed

serum calcium and potassium renal function

src.q: Glucophage SR may be used as monotherapy or in combination with other oral antidiabetic agents, or with insulin.

src.q: Reduction in the risk or delay of the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus in adult, overweight patients with IGT* and/or IFG*, and/or increased HbA1C

src.q: Ovulation stimulation to support conception in women with PCOS.

src.q: Metformin should only be considered where intensive lifestyle modifications for 3 to 6 months have not resulted in adequate glycaemic control.
Treatment with Glucophage SR must be based on a risk score incorporating appropriate measures of glycaemic control and including evidence of high cardiovascular risk

items.t: Switching from immediate-release metformin above 2000 mg daily to prolonged-release is not recommended.

src.q: In patients treated with metformin at a dose above 2000 mg daily, switching to Glucophage SR is not recommended.

items.t: Start 500 mg or 850 mg two or three times daily during or after meals. Adjust after 10 to 15 days by blood glucose; slow increase helps GI tolerance. Maximum 3 g daily in 3 divided doses (normal renal function, GFR ≥ 90 mL/min).
items.tag: Type 2 diabetes, adults: monotherapy or with other oral antidiabetics

src.q: The usual starting dose is 500 mg or 850 mg metformin hydrochloride 2 or 3 times daily given during or after meals. After 10 to 15 days the dose should be adjusted on the basis of blood glucose measurements.
A slow increase of dose may improve gastrointestinal tolerability.
The maximum recommended dose of metformin hydrochloride is 3 g daily, taken as 3 divided doses.

items.t: With insulin: usual starting dose 500 mg or 850 mg two or three times daily; insulin dose adjusted by blood glucose.

src.q: Metformin hydrochloride is given at the usual starting dose of 500 mg or 850 mg 2 or 3 times daily, while insulin dosage is adjusted on the basis of blood glucose measurements.

items.t: Start 500 mg once daily (with the evening meal). Increase by 500 mg every 10 to 15 days to a maximum of 2000 mg once daily with the evening meal. If not controlled, consider 1000 mg twice daily with food; if still not controlled, switch to standard tablets up to 3000 mg daily. Patients already on metformin: start at the equivalent daily dose.
items.tag: Type 2 diabetes, adults: monotherapy or with other oral antidiabetics

src.q: The usual starting dose is one tablet of Glucophage SR 500 mg once daily.
Dosage increases should be made in increments of 500mg every 10-15 days, up to a maximum of 2000mg once daily with the evening meal.
If glycaemic control is not achieved on Glucophage SR 2000mg once daily, Glucophage SR 1000mg twice daily should be considered, with both doses being given with food.
In patients already treated with metformin tablets, the starting dose of Glucophage SR should be equivalent to the daily dose of metformin immediate release tablets.

items.t: With insulin: usual start 500 mg once daily; insulin dose adjusted by blood glucose.

src.q: The usual starting dose of Glucophage SR is one 500 mg tablet once daily, while insulin dosage is adjusted on the basis of blood glucose measurements.

items.t: Start 500 mg once daily with the evening meal; adjust after 10 to 15 days. Maximum 2000 mg once daily with the evening meal. Review glycaemic status and risk factors every 3 to 6 months.
items.tag: Reduction in risk/delay of type 2 diabetes, adults

src.q: The therapy should be initiated with one tablet Glucophage SR 500 mg once daily with the evening meal.
